outcomes.text: Explain what research was done on the chosen stimulus and how it shaped the development of the drama or design.
Use research to inform creative decisions when devising a piece of drama.
Examine the social, cultural or historical context of the chosen stimulus.
Explain how research affected your artistic intentions.
Show how an idea develops from first thoughts to a finished, realised form.
Develop an idea from a simple stage to a more complex one.
Plan, create and structure a piece of drama.
Select ideas that make engaging drama.
Make plans for the structure and form of an artefact: set, costume, lighting or sound.
Describe how workshops move the development of a performance forward.
Plan for effective use of rehearsals and rehearse for a performance to an audience.
Edit and adapt work in progress in response to new ideas or developments.
Clearly document the development of the performance in a portfolio during devising.
Communicate meaning to an audience through engaging drama.
Refine and amend work so that clear dramatic intentions reach the audience.
Apply performance or design skills in a performance for an audience.

subtopics.title: Evaluating the devising process and outcome

outcomes.text: Examine the process of creating drama in detail and measure its impact on a live audience.
Analyse and evaluate decisions and choices made while creating the drama.
Explain changes made to the drama in relation to artistic intentions and intended audience impact.
Evaluate the final piece of devised drama.
Use accurate subject-specific terminology.
Work collaboratively to create, develop, perform and evaluate a devised piece as performer or designer.
Choose a performance role or a design role (lighting, sound, combined lighting and sound, set, costume) and keep to it for the component.
Describe the stimulus types offered, such as historic event, music, news article, painting, person, photograph, poem, prose, sculpture and song.
Study two extracts from one performance text and read the whole text.
Explain why each extract is significant in the context of the whole text.
Describe the structure of the whole text and where the extracts sit within it.
Explain the social, cultural or historical context of the text.
Identify features of the text: genre, structure, character, form and style, dialogue and stage directions.
Describe the intention of the playwright and how to interpret the text so it is communicated.
Describe artistic intentions for a performance and set them out in a concept pro forma.
Explain the semiotics of drama and the skills of a performer or designer.
Explain performance and theatrical conventions and how texts are presented to an audience.
Interpret character through voice, movement and language.
Use performance space effectively and explain the relationship between performer and audience.
Explain the semiotics of theatre as shown by the text studied.
Explain how the different aspects of design affect the whole creative experience for performers and audience.
Apply knowledge of genre, style and theatrical conventions to performing or designing the extracts.
Develop a character or design and show how it interacts with other characters or stage artefacts.
Explain the importance of rehearsal, including time management and preparation.
Use rehearsals effectively to rehearse or make, and to adapt and refine performance or design.
As a performer, give a complete performance of both extracts with lines learnt, skills used and the audience engaged.
As a designer, present complete realised designs for both extracts, with final artefacts, models or sets finished.
Demonstrate the principles underpinning your response to the extracts through performance or design.

topics.title: Section A: Studying a performance text

outcomes.text: Explain the social, historical (time set and period written) and cultural contexts of the chosen text.
Define how these contexts affect the chosen performance text.
Describe the theatrical conventions of the period in which the text was created.
Identify the text's genres, structure, characters, form and style, setting, plot and subplot, dialogue and stage directions.
Identify how a range of genres may have informed the characteristics of the text.
Explore the characteristics of the text through practical work and explain their impact.
Choose examples from your own practical study that show understanding of the full range of characteristics.
Explain how meaning is communicated through performance space and spatial relationships on stage.
Explain how meaning is communicated through the relationship between performers and audience.
Explain how meaning is communicated through the design of set, props, costume, lighting and sound.
Explain how an actor's vocal and physical interpretation of character communicates meaning.
Identify how performance conventions communicate meaning in the text.

topics.title: Section A: Development of drama and performance

outcomes.text: Describe contemporary staging types: apron, black box, in the round, promenade, proscenium arch, site specific, thrust, traverse.
Describe the roles of theatre makers: actors, choreographer, costume designer, director, lighting designer, lyricist, playwright, set designer, sound designer, stage managers, understudy.
Evaluate the roles theatre makers play in developing, performing and responding to a text.
State advantages and disadvantages of decisions in directing, acting and designing for a performance.
Describe acting skills: blocking, characterisation and improvisation.
Describe vocal techniques an actor might use to communicate a role.
Explain communication through body language, facial expression and gesture, and the use of semiotics.
Explain the design and use of sets, including composite and non-naturalistic sets.
Explain how costume, hair and makeup, and masks help develop character.
Describe the use of contemporary light, sound and media technology in performance.
Explain how performance styles affect the direction, acting and design of a performance.
Define features of a performance text: acts and scenes, antagonist, protagonist, character, dialogue, duologue, monologue, flashback, plot and subplot, stage directions.
Apply knowledge of the development of drama and performance to the studied text.
Use appropriate subject-specific terminology about theatre and the work of theatre makers.
Explain how genre is used in live performance to communicate meaning.
Discuss, analyse and evaluate how meaning is created and communicated in live theatre.
Analyse and evaluate the acting, design and characteristics of the performance text seen.
Evaluate the work of others and draw considered conclusions.
